summary: A 4-plate music plate for an existing folding music-stand holder (tapered sheet-metal channel, M6 stud with a thumb nut, two rivet heads). A separate V part slides into the holder; its 50 mm tongue sits behind the centre plate, held by 2 dovetail keys in grooves in the plate's back and 2 printed M6 countersunk bolts with printed nuts. The 170 x 170 centre plate and two 170 x 170 extenders (dropped on from the top on dovetail rails) make a 430 x 170 mm plate with a 10 mm lip and a hex mesh. PLA on an A1 mini, one part per plate.

assumptions: A1: PLA on a Bambu A1 mini (180 x 180 x 180), 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, no supports. If the bed differs, the 170 mm long centre plate (plate + tab) may not fit.
A3: the channel's usable inner widths are the user's 37.6 and 30.6 (not the outer 44.4 / 37.9). The tab is made 0.3 mm smaller per side on both widths.
A6: all extenders are a left/right pair, printed once each.

A7: the model files lay the three parts out side by side (extenders moved 50 mm out) so the drawings and the viewer show a print layout; the assembled position is in the datum and the section views. Slicers re-place the parts anyway.
A8 (rev 2): centre plate mesh uses the same hole size, rib and border (D34-D36), 5 columns across x = -37..37; it stops D36 away from the peg-hole zones and above the lip.

A9 (rev 3): from the insertion sweep, the tab is 65 mm and the plates 105 mm tall, so the plate bottom edge rests on the channel top and the tab tip stops 0.4 mm short of the curved support. A channel of 66.9 mm leaves 0.9 mm at the tip.

A10 (rev 4): the extenders drop on from the top. 2 dovetail rails per extender (5 mm neck, 8 mm head, 2.4 mm high) slide down into grooves in the centre plate's back face; the grooves are closed at the bottom (y = 8), so gravity seats the extender and the paper weight loads the joint in compression. The groove leaves a 1.4 mm front skin on the 4 mm plate. No snap detent: add a dab of glue or a small bump later if it lifts out.
A5 (replaced in rev 4): the push-in pegs were dropped.

A12 (rev 7): the solid tab was pushed up by the stud on the printed test, so the slot is back, narrowed to the measured M6 stud. The nut screws onto the stud through the slot; a 2 mm recess lets it reach more thread. How far the stud stands out was not measured.

A13 (rev 7): the printed nut assumes M6 x 1.0 (coarse). Its thread flanks are 60 degree overhangs (ISO profile), which the A1 mini prints at this size; OVERHANG_LIMIT is 60 for that reason and the plates were checked at 45.

A14 (rev 8): photo 131610 shows the raised collar round the stud hole and the two rivet domes. The narrow slot is sized for the collar (7.4 mm) and both slot ends run 1 mm past the measured positions.

A15 (rev 9): with the slot closed at the tip, the stud (bolt) must be taken out before the tab slides in, then pushed back through the slot from behind and the nut fitted. The bridge rides over the domes and the collar: if the domes are taller than 3 mm, the relief must be deeper.
A16 (rev 10): the final 3MF has 3 plates (centre, left extender, right extender) for Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer; the fit test and the nut are only in the separate test-plate 3MF.
A17 (rev 11): tab widened 1 mm per side after the physical fit test; the sweep checks the stud, collar, domes and the stop, and the side walls were checked by the user's test print.

A18 (rev 12): the V is a separate part. The chosen 'thickened pad with a socket on the back of the centre plate' cannot print with the plate's back on the bed (the pad would stick out below the bed face, a back socket needs a 40 mm flat roof), so the V's tongue sits behind the plate and goes into it with 2 dovetail keys in grooves (2.4 mm deep) instead, plus 2 printed M6 bolts. Printed M6 threads are weak: the keys carry the load, the bolts only clamp.

Keep the sloped outer edge on the extenders, or use a full-height square now that the hex mesh saves the material?
